title: Farewell to Principal Agha Sadiq Hussain Shah
titleOriginal: محترم آغا صادق حسین شاہ پرنسپل کالج
takeaway: Good leaders bring spring with them, and take a little of it when they go.
scene: A four-line farewell to a college principal, Agha Sadiq Hussain Shah, who was leaving his post.

original: محفل دی جان تے شمع علم دی منیا ایتھوں جا رہے ہین
پہلے ٹھنڈ کلیجے پا کے ہن سل سینے تے لا رہے نیں
transliteration: Mehfil di jaan te shamaa ilm di, manniya, ethon ja rahe hain
Pehle thand kaleje paa ke, hun sil seene te la rahe nain
translation: The life of the gathering, the acknowledged candle of learning, is leaving here.
First he brought comfort to our hearts; now he lays a heavy stone on our chests.
couplets.story: The man who brought life to every gathering, and was a 'candle of learning', is leaving. First he made everyone feel good. Now his leaving feels like a heavy stone on their chests.

original: آون دے نال آئی سی جیہڑی اودھوں رت بہاراں دی
جاون لگے نال لے گئے تاہیوں پھل کملا رہے نیں
transliteration: Aavan de naal aayi si jehri ondhon rut bahaaraan di
Jaavan lagge naal lai gaye, taahiyon phull kumla rahe nain
translation: The season of spring that came with him when he arrived,
he's taking with him as he leaves; that's why the flowers are wilting.
couplets.story: When he arrived, it was as if spring came with him. Now he's taking spring away, and that's why the flowers are drooping.

why: A short, warm example of how a good leader is missed.
prompt: Who has brought 'spring' to a place you've been, a class, a team or a home?
